name: Brixton
amenity_sentence: Fourteen pubs, eight churches and chapels, six bookmakers — and a covered market that has outlasted every wave of regeneration.

name: Stockwell
amenity_sentence: Nine pubs and fourteen cafés serving coffee in Portuguese and English, with four bookmakers taking bets in both.

name: Vauxhall
amenity_sentence: Eleven pubs, six supermarkets, and a nightclub district that operates on a different clock to the rest of south London.

name: Pimlico
amenity_sentence: Six quiet pubs and twelve cafés, two bookmakers barely visible from the street — a neighbourhood that keeps its pleasures understated.

name: Victoria
amenity_sentence: Thirty-four cafés, eighteen pubs, and nine supermarkets — a district built entirely around people who are somewhere else in their heads.

name: Green Park
amenity_sentence: Four discreet pubs, sixteen cafés priced for hotel guests, and a single bookmaker that looks slightly embarrassed to be here.

name: Oxford Circus
amenity_sentence: Forty-eight cafés, twelve pubs, and eight supermarkets competing for the attention of two hundred thousand daily passers-through.

name: Warren Street
amenity_sentence: Seven pubs and nineteen cafés serving the hospital shifts — a neighbourhood that runs on sandwiches and strong tea at any hour.

name: Euston
amenity_sentence: Sixteen pubs built around the anxiety of departure, five bookmakers for the time between trains, twenty-eight cafés that don't expect you to stay.

name: King's Cross St. Pancras
amenity_sentence: Thirty-six cafés, fourteen pubs, and a coal-yard-turned-food-market — the neighbourhood that twenty years of investment built from almost nothing.

name: Highbury & Islington
amenity_sentence: Thirteen pubs and twenty-four cafés in a postcode where the menus have changed faster than the faces — and both faster than the rents.

name: Finsbury Park
amenity_sentence: Seven places of worship, ten pubs, and twenty cafés — Eritrean, Turkish, and Irish kitchens side by side along the same hundred metres.

name: Seven Sisters
amenity_sentence: Seven bookmakers, eight pubs, six places of worship — the arithmetic of a street that measures its own odds carefully.

name: Tottenham Hale
amenity_sentence: Five pubs, six supermarkets, four bookmakers — a transport interchange surrounded by the utilitarian commerce of a place people mostly pass through.

name: Blackhorse Road
amenity_sentence: Seven pubs, three of them breweries that opened in the last decade — the quiet end of the line where something new is being tried.

name: Walthamstow Central
amenity_sentence: Nine pubs, seven places of worship, and a market a mile long — the end of the line, and a complete world in itself.
